topic: What Breaks an AI Agent After 50 Clean Demos: Production Reliability Guide (2026)

competitors.title: Ask HN: How are you testing AI agents before shipping to production?
key_points: 7 failure modes identified: hallucination under unexpected inputs, edge case collapse, prompt injection, context limit surprises, cascade failures, data integration drift, authorization confusion
Most teams test hallucination and prompt injection; almost no one systematically tests context limits, cascade failures, or data integration drift before shipping
Gartner predicted over 40% of AI agent projects will fail by 2027
January 2026: prompt injection in a customer support agent processed a $47,000 fraudulent refund
Epistemic distortion: agent gives correct-looking output but applies wrong standard of evidence

competitors.title: 12-factor Agents: Patterns of reliable LLM applications (475 points, 78 comments)
key_points: Most production AI agents are not that agentic — they're well-engineered software with LLM steps at key points

12 factors: own your prompts, own your context window, tools as structured outputs, unify execution/business state, launch/pause/resume, contact humans with tool calls, own control flow, compact errors into context, small focused agents, stateless reducer
80% quality bar is common with frameworks; getting past 80% requires reverse-engineering the framework
Best approach: take small modular concepts from agents and incorporate into existing product, not greenfield rewrite

competitors.title: Lessons from securing AI systems at runtime (agents, MCPs, LLMs)
key_points: Hard problems show up after deployment, not during model choice or prompt quality
Agents call tools nobody remembered wiring up; LLMs access internal APIs through invisible chains
Execution identity diverges from user identity; MCP servers become quiet control planes
Existing security assumptions break: static services, clear ownership, single-hop execution, pre-defined boundaries — AI violates all of these

competitors.title: Flakestorm – Chaos engineering for AI agents (local-first, open source)
key_points: Agents fail in mundane ways: typos, tone shifts, long context, malformed input, simple prompt injections
Chaos engineering approach: take golden prompt, generate adversarial mutations, run against agent, produce robustness score
Local-first using Ollama for mutation generation; works with small models like Qwen/Gemma

competitors.title: mcp-recorder – VCR.py for MCP servers. Record, replay, verify
key_points: Renamed tool parameters or tweaked descriptions silently break AI agents — all tests pass but agent behavior changes
MCP spec lacks tool versioning; no static artifact describing what a server exposes
Cassette-based testing: record full MCP interaction sequence, replay as mock server, verify against diffs
